name: REINVENT
question: Does nightly or on-demand vardenafil after bilateral nerve-sparing radical prostatectomy improve unassisted erectile recovery after treatment withdrawal?

design.population: Men aged 18–64 years with preoperative IIEF-EF score at least 26 who were scheduled for bilateral nerve-sparing radical prostatectomy.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 925–926; Results, p 927

verdictNote: The prespecified overall comparison after washout was not significant.
takeaway: After bilateral nerve-sparing prostatectomy, nightly vardenafil, on-demand vardenafil, and placebo yielded IIEF-EF scores of at least 22 after washout in 24.1%, 29.1%, and 28.9% of the modified ITT population, respectively; the primary comparison was not significant.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Montorsi F, Brock G, Lee J, et al. "Effect of Nightly versus On-Demand Vardenafil on Recovery of Erectile Function in Men Following Bilateral Nerve-Sparing Radical Prostatectomy." *Eur Urol.* 2008;54(4):924-931. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2008.06.083
reports.followUp: Nine months of randomized treatment, two-month washout, and optional two-month open-label treatment

results.measure: Proportion with IIEF-EF score at least 22 after two-month washout
results.note: Modified ITT, n=445 (143 nightly, 149 on demand, 153 placebo), with a washout IIEF-EF measurement; last observation carried forward. Prespecified overall three-group test at p<0.05 was not significant. Exact primary P value, effect estimate, and confidence interval were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 926; Results and Fig. 3, pp 927–928

results.measure: IIEF-EF score and SEP3 success over nine-month treatment period

values.nightly: 32.0% with IIEF-EF at least 22 at double-blind LOCF; 34.5% mean per-patient SEP3 success overall
values.ondemand: 48.2% with IIEF-EF at least 22 at double-blind LOCF; 45.9% mean per-patient SEP3 success overall
values.placebo: 24.8% with IIEF-EF at least 22 at double-blind LOCF; 25.0% mean per-patient SEP3 success overall

effect.p: IIEF-EF at least 22: 0.0001 on demand vs placebo, 0.0065 on demand vs nightly; SEP3: <0.0001 on demand vs placebo, 0.0344 nightly vs placebo

results.note: Secondary comparisons were nominal; efficacy analyses used the mITT population. At double-blind LOCF, arm n was 143 nightly, 149 on demand, and 152 placebo; for overall double-blind SEP3, arm n was 135, 144, and 147, respectively. Confidence intervals were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods and Results, pp 926–927; Figs. 3–4, pp 928–929

harms.label: Any adverse event during double-blind treatment
Common adverse events during double-blind treatment
Discontinuation due to adverse events
harms.note: 39 patients overall; 17/207 nightly, 12/204 on demand, and 10/206 placebo discontinued due to adverse events.
harms.locator: Full text, Results, Adverse events, p 929

delivery.label: Treatment sequence
delivery.value: Randomized within 14 days of bilateral nerve-sparing prostatectomy: 10 mg nightly vardenafil (reducible to 5 mg) plus on-demand placebo; on-demand vardenafil starting at 10 mg (titrated to 5 or 20 mg) plus nightly placebo; or double placebo for nine months. Two months of single-blind placebo washout without devices followed, then optional two-month open-label on-demand vardenafil starting at 10 mg (adjustable to 5 or 20 mg after one month).
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Study design, pp 925–926

delivery.label: Participant disposition and analysis sets
delivery.value: 997 screened, 628 randomized, 617 in the safety population, 599 in ITT, 445 in modified ITT for efficacy, and 423 completed the study.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, Study population and baseline demographics, p 927; Fig. 2, p 927
